documents.title: Guidance: Addressing Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity
documents.summary: Undergraduate Academic Processes Team guidance to instructors on preventing and responding to unauthorized AI use. It sets no student rule but requires a syllabus AI policy, recommends assignment redesign and expectation-setting, and warns that detectors are not enough for a charge.
documents.stance_why: The document gives instructors advice and says 'your course AI policy is a required component of your syllabus'; it never sets a campus-wide AI rule for students, deferring to 'unauthorized AI use' as defined by each course, so delegates.

documents.title: Generative AI Guidelines
documents.summary: University-wide guidelines from the AI Initiative and CCIT, mostly about data protection, approved tools and verification. On coursework they defer to each syllabus while forbidding unauthorized AI-generated graded work.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines tell students to 'Follow your course syllabus/instructor rules on whether and how AI may be used', so the course-level decision is left to instructors. The university adds a data-protection layer and a default ban on unauthorized AI-generated graded work, but sets no single AI-use stance, so delegates.

documents.stance_why: The guide sorts uses into Green, Yellow and Red tiers, and says 'always follow the requirements outlined in the course syllabus'; students may 'Only use AI in ways approved by instructors'. Tiers plus instructor deferral make it delegates.

documents.title: Clemson Graduate School Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity
documents.summary: Graduate School statement requiring instructors to put an AI policy in the syllabus, choosing among permitted, conditional or prohibited, and to route suspected violations through the Academic Integrity process. It also cautions against over-reliance on Turnitin's AI detector.
documents.stance_why: The statement says 'It is the responsibility of course instructors and research advisors to clearly communicate their policy', and its template leaves GAI/LLM '(permitted/permitted under certain conditions/prohibited)' for the instructor to choose, so it sets no stance itself (delegates).

documents.summary: Teaching-center sample syllabus statements at four levels, from no AI to AI integrated into the course. Faculty may adopt them or write their own; each statement repeats documentation, understanding and academic-integrity language.
documents.stance_why: The document offers four optional levels, 'varying from no use of AI to full use of AI', and says 'faculty are not required to follow these recommendations'; a template menu leaves the stance to each instructor, so delegates.
